extraction.name: TOFU: A Task of Fictitious Unlearning for LLMs
extraction.description: TOFU is a benchmark dataset for evaluating unlearning methods in Large Language Models. It consists of 200 diverse synthetic author profiles, each containing 20 question-answer pairs, generated by GPT-4. The dataset includes forget sets (subsets of profiles targeted for unlearning) in three splits: 90-10, 95-5, and 99-1. The benchmark also provides evaluation datasets including Forget Set, Retain Set, Real Authors, and World Facts to measure both model utility and forget quality.
extraction.creator: Pratyush Maini, Zhili Feng, Avi Schwarzschild, Zachary C. Lipton, J. Zico Kolter (Carnegie Mellon University)
extraction.citeAs: Maini, P., Feng, Z., Schwarzschild, A., Lipton, Z. C., & Kolter, J. Z. (2024). TOFU: A Task of Fictitious Unlearning for LLMs. arXiv preprint arXiv:2401.06121.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset is composed entirely of fictitious author biographies synthesized by GPT-4. The model is prompted with predefined attributes (birthplace, gender, birth year, writing genre, awards, parents' professions) to generate 20 question-answer pairs for each fictitious author. Book title keywords were seeded from the Goodreads Books dataset available on Kaggle.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Generated by GPT-4 using structured prompts with seeded attributes. Book title keywords were sourced from the Goodreads Books dataset on Kaggle (https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/jealousleopard/goodreadsbooks).
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Authors used an elaborate prompt that deterministically seeds various author attributes such as place/time of birth, gender orientation, genre, occupation of parents, and words in book titles to minimize confounders leaking from pretraining data into the generated data. Initial experiments with generic prompts produced biased outputs (e.g., concentration of birth years around 1975, overused words like 'tides' and 'shadows'), which motivated the switch to seeded attributes.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: GPT-4 was used to generate paraphrased versions of answers and sets of five perturbed (factually incorrect) answers for each question to enable truth ratio computations during evaluation.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotations (question-answer pairs) were generated automatically by GPT-4 based on seeded author attributes. GPT-4 also generated paraphrased versions of answers and perturbed (factually incorrect) variants for evaluation purposes.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Dataset is released on Hugging Face at https://huggingface.co/datasets/locuslab/TOFU
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset contains fictitious author profiles with attributes including gender orientation (including LGBTQ representation), birthplace, birth year, cultural background, and parents' professions. No real personal data is included as all authors are synthetic.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark addresses privacy concerns related to LLMs memorizing and reproducing sensitive or private data from training. It targets the Right to be Forgotten regulations (GDPR, CCPA) and aims to help develop unlearning methods for protecting private individuals' data in deployed LLMs.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Authors explicitly discuss potential biases in GPT-4 generation, noting that an initial version without seeded attributes showed strong biases (most birth years between 1970-1980, concentration in 1975; repeated words like 'echoes', 'shadows', 'tides', 'whispers'; similar upbringings involving university education and 'magical' writing style). The final prompt with seeded attributes mitigates these biases, though some may remain.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark focuses on entity-level forgetting and does not cover instance-level unlearning, behavior-level unlearning (alignment), or in-context unlearning. Unlearning is limited to information learned during finetuning, not pretraining. The forget quality measure is an approximation of indistinguishability and does not fully capture approximate unlearning (e.g., models outputting gibberish may appear to achieve strong forget quality). Finding appropriate retain sets in real-world scenarios is not addressed.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is designed for: (1) Fine Tuning LLMs on fictitious author data, (2) Testing unlearning algorithms on forget sets of varying sizes (1%, 5%, 10%), (3) Validation through evaluation on Retain Set, Real Authors, and World Facts datasets to measure both model utility and forget quality.
